title: A Home for Two Tiny Leaves
originalStory: A little library book wriggled out of its basket to find the green sprout in its story. The librarian showed it a pot where a seed had just grown two tiny leaves. She opened the book to the matching picture, and the little book felt right at home.
visualBible:
Pip: magical little library book, small square shape, butter-yellow cover with a green sprout picture, two gentle ink-dot eyes and a tiny curved mouth on the cover, cream pages, no arms or legs, no clothes.
Ms. Willow: adult woman librarian, normal human ears, warm brown skin, short curly silver hair, round purple glasses, lavender cardigan, dark blue trousers, flat brown shoes, adult-sized.

pages.text: Pip, a little library book, wriggled out of a basket on the soft reading rug. Somewhere beyond those cream-colored pages, perhaps the green sprout from the story was growing. “Two tiny leaves,” whispered Pip, “where are you?”
pages.illustrationScene: Soft watercolor, Sulu Boya mood, with warm washes and delicate paper texture. Pip is alone in a cozy library reading nook, just outside a shallow basket resting directly on a soft rug. Pip’s butter-yellow cover, green sprout picture, ink-dot eyes, and tiny mouth are visible. Low bookshelves frame the quiet, curious moment; no other characters are present.

pages.text: Pip shuffled across the carpet, past a green cushion that was much too plump to be a leaf. Ms. Willow knelt nearby and asked, “What are you looking for, little book?” “Something small and green that might know my story,” said Pip.
pages.illustrationScene: Soft watercolor, Sulu Boya mood. On the broad carpet beside the library’s low reading bench, Pip rests near a plump green cushion while Ms. Willow kneels comfortably close, listening. Pip has a butter-yellow cover with a sprout picture and a small ink-drawn face. Ms. Willow has short curly silver hair, normal human ears, purple glasses, a lavender cardigan, dark blue trousers, and flat brown shoes. The composition is intimate and welcoming.

pages.text: “I think I know someone,” Ms. Willow said, carrying Pip to a low table in a patch of sunlight. In a little pot, a seed had just grown two tiny leaves. Ms. Willow opened Pip to the matching picture, and Pip whispered, “Oh—you’re here.”
pages.illustrationScene: Soft watercolor, Sulu Boya mood. In the library’s sunny plant corner, Ms. Willow sits beside a low, rounded wooden table and gently holds Pip open next to a small stable pot containing a fresh sprout with exactly two tiny green leaves. Pip’s cream-colored page shows a matching two-leaf sprout, and the butter-yellow cover is visible beneath the pages. Ms. Willow’s silver curls, purple glasses, lavender cardigan, dark blue trousers, flat brown shoes, and normal human ears match her established appearance. Focus on the quiet discovery; no extra characters or gardening tools.

pages.text: Ms. Willow settled Pip on the low table beside the pot, with the sprout picture still open. “You can keep each other company,” she said. Sunlight warmed the paper, the two little leaves leaned toward the light, and Pip felt right at home.
pages.illustrationScene: Soft watercolor, Sulu Boya mood, in a close, peaceful composition at the library’s low rounded table. Pip lies open beside the small stable pot, with the pictured sprout and the real two-leaf sprout facing the same soft sunlight. Ms. Willow sits beside the table, one hand resting gently near Pip; her silver curls, purple glasses, normal human ears, lavender cardigan, dark blue trousers, and flat brown shoes remain consistent. The pot and book are comfortably separated on the tabletop. The mood is tender belonging.
